control.note: The Senate was tied 37–37; Republicans organized it with the votes of Readjuster William Mahone and Vice President Arthur.
Republicans won more seats, but Democrats organized the House with third-party votes and kept Speaker Champ Clark.
Republicans won 218 seats, but deaths and special elections before Congress convened in December 1931 gave Democrats control; John Nance Garner became Speaker.
Republicans organized the Senate with Vice President Nixon's tie-breaking vote; deaths shifted the balance during the Congress.

The Senate was split 50–50: Democrats controlled it for 17 days in January 2001 (with Vice President Gore), then Republicans (with Vice President Cheney), then Democrats again from June 2001 after Senator Jim Jeffords left the Republican Party.
Democrats held the majority, 51–49, counting two independents who caucused with them.
The Senate was split 50–50; Democrats controlled it with Vice President Kamala Harris's tie-breaking vote, counting two independents who caucused with them.
Democrats held the majority, 51–49, counting three independents who caucused with them.
